mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.3% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-0.3% monthly payroll growth for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing output and lower corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding -0.4%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% and a decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below -2% signals strong demand for housing financed by debt, which boosts construction and related equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods meeting the HOUST and RSAFS trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months while the federal funds rate remains below 2%, it signals a delayed policy response to inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes of high inflation and low rates meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for six consecutive months signals an extremely tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of six consecutive months with UNRATE below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real personal consumption expenditures growth (proxied by GDPC1 quarter-over-quarter change) and S&P 500 20-day forward returns, such that above-consensus GDP growth forecasts imply higher equity valuations.
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive correlation between GDPC1 QoQ growth and S&P 500 20-day forward returns in out-of-sample walk-forward testing.
